proposed_title: Preprint proposes trajectory-aware estimation for software-agent benchmarks
what_happened: Fresh Cloud GETs retrieved the exact arXiv API record and abstract page for preprint 2609.01603, submitted 1 September 2026. The authors propose PTA-IRT, which uses historical execution trajectories when selecting calibration tasks and estimating agent ability.
key_facts: ABSTRACT_ONLY: the authors report better score and ranking recovery than prior IRT baselines under low calibration budgets across four software-engineering benchmarks.
FACT: the arXiv record labels the manuscript under review and links code and data.
UNKNOWN: full methods, effect sizes, benchmark leakage, code, data, conflicts and replication were not inspected.

primary_sources.attribution: Duan et al. arXiv abstract record
primary_sources.claim_supported: Bibliographic status and the authors' abstract-level method and performance claims
primary_sources.independence: Author-submitted preprint record; not peer review or replication

primary_sources.attribution: arXiv abstract page for Efficient SWE Agent Benchmarking via Trajectory-Aware Evaluation
primary_sources.independence: Second representation of the same preprint, not an independent source

contradictory_evidence: The claims come from one under-review preprint and have not been independently replicated.
Abstract-level comparisons cannot establish robustness outside the four reported benchmarks.
uncertainty: High confidence in identity and status; low confidence in scientific conclusions until full-text and replication review.
context: This is current computer-science research, not a peer-reviewed result. Efficient benchmark estimation may trade evaluation cost against accuracy.
why_it_matters: Agent evaluations are expensive, so reliable lower-cost estimation would be useful if the result survives scrutiny.
strategic_angle: HOLD pending full-text methods, code/data inspection and independent context.
